We are going to see answers to a bunch of questions, each of whose possible outcomes are radically different, and that will probably have significant impacts on the world's status quo:

Who will be president of the United States?

It's easy to see how a victory for Mr. Trump would be impactful both for US domestic and foreign policy... but if he wins, how did he win, and who did he win against?

Will the Democrat party ditch Mrs. Clinton at the last moment and endorse Mr. Sanders, who will then go on to lose? It could happen - especially if the FBI's investigation into her alleged misuse of State Department e-mails continues to bear fruit.

Will Mr. Sanders, having lost the primary, run as an independent and ensure Mr. Trump's victory?

Or perhaps President Obama pardons Mrs. Clinton, and she runs in the general election with the scandal (but no conviction) hanging around her neck.

Or perhaps Mrs. Clinton wins. How would she have won, and against whom? A popular-vote victory against Mr. Trump? Or might the Republican party ditch Mr. Trump for some other candidate and ensure their own defeat?

Americans have been freaking out over elections more and more in the past few cycles, but they always get over it. This one will probably take longer, though.

Furthermore, the US' two-party political system itself seems fairly stable, and the time between shifts in which two parties those are seems to have been increasing - but this election cycle seems like the closest in a long time to one that might actually see the fall of one of the two parties (and its replacement by another) - and that would be an effect that would last far beyond the presidential election season.

Who will rule Venezuela?

Inflation runs rampant; food runs out, the government's credibility is crumbling and those that have a means to leave are leaving. Historically, these events (especially the runaway inflation) in a country precede a war, out of which a new government forms. There's going to be a war in Venezuela - but what will happen to the government?

The United States has a long history of helping free governments emerge out of countries in conflict, especially those with large oil reserves (Venezuela has the largest confirmed oil reserve of any country on earth). Will the United States try again in Venezuela, after Hugo Chavez refused to play nice for so long?

A notable exception where inflation ran rampant but the government survived is the US' own Great Depression - but only by the saving grace of the financial impetus of a global war. Will Venezuela be so "lucky" to have their war be a world war, instead of a civil war?

Will Britain Remain in the EU?

This vote is up soon! But there's talk that the British parliament may accept a "Brexit" but still contribute to the EU financially and/or in other ways, circumventing the will of the people.

Will Brexit pass? Will Parliament attempt to shaft their people? Would the Brits accept this? There's really only one way that it doesn't get ugly for someone: Landslide victory for "remain."

If Britain leaves, the figurative (and perhaps literal) keystone of the EU is gone and the Eurozone's crumble accelerates. If Britain stays by a hair, internal unrest continues and it smolders slowly with the rest of Europe.

Will Europe stay ethnically European?

So far, ethnically-European EU citizens are still holding the reigns of Europe's governments, though they are accommodating non-citizen non-Europeans across the board.

How long until non-European non-citizens are in the government buildings, making the policy and decisions? Will today's Europeans change the path their countries are on before that happens?

What will a Europe that doesn't change course look like? What will the UN look like?

How will Putin's Russia handle a Muslim Europe?

Remember what Putin was up to before the Muslim invasion of Europe? He was helping Crimeans in Ukraine live in the country they really wanted to live in! Also, securing a year-round port free of ice for the Russian navy.

Aside from intervening in Syria, he's been more or less quiet while Europe struggles.

If Europe falls to the invaders, might Putin assist in the liberation and protection of the EU citizens with whom his Russia allied itself in the UN? Re-establish the Soviet bloc and drive out the invaders... and keep the troops around indefinitely, you know, to help rebuild, and in case they come back?

Perhaps that could ignite world war that saves the current Venezuelan government...
